*Gone With the Wind* received generally positive reviews upon its release on December 15, 1939. While the casting was widely praised, the long running time received criticism. At the [12th Academy Awards](/wiki/12th_Academy_Awards "12th Academy Awards"), *Gone with the Wind* received ten [Academy Awards](/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") (eight competitive, two honorary) from thirteen nominations, including wins for [Best Picture](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"), [Best Director](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") (Fleming), [Best Adapted Screenplay](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay") (posthumously awarded to Sidney Howard), [Best Actress](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress") (Leigh), and [Best Supporting Actress](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress") ([Hattie McDaniel](/wiki/Hattie_McDaniel "Hattie McDaniel"), becoming the first [African American](/wiki/African_American "African American") to win an Academy Award). It set records for the total number of wins and nominations at the time.

*Gone with the Wind* was immensely popular when first released. It became the [highest-earning film made up to that point](/wiki/Timeline_of_highest-grossing_films "Timeline of highest-grossing films") and held the record for over a quarter of a century. When [adjusted for monetary inflation](/wiki/Real_versus_nominal_value_(economics) "Real versus nominal value (economics)"), it is still [the highest-grossing film in history](/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films_adjusted_for_inflation "List of highest-grossing films adjusted for inflation"). It was re-released periodically throughout the 20th century and became ingrained in popular culture. Although the film has been criticized as [historical negationism](/wiki/Historical_negationism "Historical negationism"), glorifying [slavery](/wiki/Slavery_in_the_United_States "Slavery in the United States") and the [Lost Cause of the Confederacy](/wiki/Lost_Cause_

A three-year-old male Alaskan husky

The Alaskan husky has selectively been bred specifically for its athletic performance.[[14]](#cite_note-:4-14)[[5]](#cite_note-:2-5) As such, its level of athletic ability, as well as [anabolic](/wiki/Anabolism "Anabolism") efficiency are far greater than the average domesticated dog, especially in endurance feats. Distance-specialist Alaskan huskies out-speed most animals and all other types of sled dogs when running distances of 50 miles or greater, even while pulling moderately sized loads.[[5]](#cite_note-:2-5) Studies on the metabolic capabilities in working Alaskan husky sled dogs reveal that their system transitions to utilization of low-glucose energy sources (from high-glycogen carbohydrates) early on during long periods of travel, and their reliance on these low-glucose fuels (such as those higher in fats and proteins) continue and even extend to become more pronounced after working for longer periods.[[14]](#cite_note-:4-14) A good appetite is a highly desirable trait, and is emphasized in breeding choices.[[15]](#cite_note-:0-15)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/Idol_swingley.jpg/250px-Idol_swingley.jpg)](/wiki/File:Idol_swingley.jpg)

Five-year-old male Alaskan husky from championship distance racing lines

Like most working sled dogs, Alaskan huskies are capable of pulling far greater than their own body weight in load while in harness. Sprint teams of Alaskan huskies are capable of speeds of up to 28 mph (45 km/h),[[16]](#cite_note-16) whereas distance-specialist teams have completed 938 mile (1510 km) races in just 8 days, 3 hours, 40 minutes, and 13 seconds with time including 40 hours of mandatory rests and other routine rests on the trail.[[17]](#cite_note-17)

* [Draco Malfoy](/wiki/Draco_Malfoy "Draco Malfoy") is a slim, pale boy who speaks in a bored drawl. He is arrogant about his skill in Quidditch, and despises anyone who is not a pure-blood wizard and wizards who do not share his views. His parents had supported Voldemort, but changed sides after the dark wizard's disappearance, claiming they had been [bewitched](/wiki/Imperius_Curse "Imperius Curse"). Draco avoids direct confrontations and tries to get Harry and his friends into trouble.
* [Oliver Wood](/wiki/Oliver_Wood_(Harry_Potter) "Oliver Wood (Harry Potter)") is a fifth year who acts as Harry's Quidditch captain and keeper for the Gryffindor Quidditch team.
* [Professor Quirrell](/wiki/Professor_Quirrell "Professor Quirrell") is a twitching, stammering, and nervous man who teaches Defence Against the Dark Arts. Reputedly he was a brilliant scholar, but his nerve was shattered by an encounter with vampires. Quirrell wears a turban to conceal the fact that he is voluntarily possessed by Voldemort, whose face appears on the back of Quirrell's head.
* Professor [Severus Snape](/wiki/Severus_Snape "Severus Snape"), who has a hooked nose, sallow complexion, and greasy black hair, teaches Potions, but would prefer to teach Defence Against the Dark Arts. Snape favours pupils in his own House of Slytherin, and appears to delight in humiliating those from other houses, especially Harry. Several incidents, beginning with the shooting pain in Harry's scar during the start-of-term feast, lead Harry and his friends to think Snape is aiding Voldemort.
* [Argus Filch](/wiki/Argus_Filch "Argus Filch"), the school caretaker who knows the school's [secret passages](/wiki/Hogwarts#Passages "Hogwarts") better than anyone else except, perhaps, the Weasley twins. His cat, Mrs. Norris, aids his constant hunt for misbehaving pupils.

Main article: [History of the Argentina national football team](/wiki/History_of_the_Argentina_national_football_team "History of the Argentina national football team")

Further information: [Football in Argentina](/wiki/Football_in_Argentina "Football in Argentina")

[The first ever match](/wiki/1902_Uruguay_v_Argentina_football_match "1902 Uruguay v Argentina football match") Argentina played was against [Uruguay](/wiki/Uruguay_national_football_team "Uruguay national football team") on 20 June 1902, in [Montevideo](/wiki/Montevideo "Montevideo").[[note 2]](#cite_note-albion-25) It was the first international match for both sides, and Argentina won 6–0.[[4]](#cite_note-First_match-5)[[7]](#cite_note-barnade-8) During the first years of Argentina's existence, the team only played [friendly matches](/wiki/Exhibition_game "Exhibition game") against other South American teams. The reasons for this varied, including long travel times between countries and the outbreak of [World War I](/wiki/World_War_I "World War I").[[19]](#cite_note-26)

Bank of America cut around 16,000 jobs in a quicker fashion by the end of 2012 as revenue continued to decline because of new regulations and a slow economy. The locations were converted to Huntington National Bank branches in September.[[98]](#cite_note-98)

As part of its new strategy Bank of America is focused on growing its mobile banking platform. As of 2014, Bank of America has 31 million active online users and 16 million mobile users.
